questions.question: Will these scores affect real hiring decisions in the EU, and who reviews the shortlist?
Are these predictions used only in testing, or to select actual applicants?
Is this used to identify someone against a gallery, or solely to verify a claimed identity, and where is it deployed?
Whose faces are processed, for what purpose, and in what deployment setting?
Where are customers told they are interacting with AI before the first reply?
Do you provide this chatbot under your own name, or deploy another provider's system?
How are synthetic outputs marked as AI-generated and detected by downstream users?
Which content types are generated, and what is your provider or deployer role?
Which real decisions use these predictions, who is affected, and where will the system be deployed?
Is this an AI model or a deterministic transformation, and what is the intended use of its predictions?
Where did the training data come from, how were labels checked, and what cleaning or exclusion steps were documented?
Which bias tests and mitigation steps were performed on the training and validation data for the affected applicant groups?
How were missing values, label errors and representativeness checked for the intended applicant population?
Which deployment population and environment were used when selecting the training and evaluation data?
Who can inspect and override the shortlist, and how can they pause or reverse an automated decision?
Which held-out evaluation results and acceptance thresholds support using these scores for the intended hiring task?
Which accuracy metrics and limitations are communicated to the people using these model outputs?
How are loaded model artifacts and prediction inputs checked for tampering or poisoning?
Where are risks from intended use and foreseeable misuse recorded, evaluated and reviewed over time?
What predefined metrics and thresholds are used to test the model before deployment?
Where are the model version, intended use, training choices and evaluation evidence documented?
Which model version, input reference, score and reviewer action are logged for each decision?
What limitations and instructions do the people interpreting these scores receive?
Who provides this system under their name and is responsible for its development and documentation?
Who operates this system and assigns trained people with authority to review its decisions?
Who controls the live input data and checks that it represents the intended population?
How are people informed that this system contributes to decisions affecting them?
How are viewers informed when this output is a deepfake rather than authentic content?
When and in what accessible form is the AI disclosure shown to the affected person?
Where are the training objective, hyperparameter choices and their trade-offs documented and evaluated?
Where is the datasheet recording training methodology, dataset provenance, selection, labelling and cleaning?
For special-category data used specifically for bias auditing, how is access restricted and deletion triggered after correction or retention expiry?
